candidates.statement: Order service returns HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders, which the gateway surfaces as 502 on POST /v1/checkout. Traces and logs show every checkout failure is caused by an upstream 500 from order, not by gateway faults.
candidates.uncertainty: Evidence localizes the fault to order's 500 responses but does not reveal the internal cause (db pool, redis, payment) inside order.

report.explanation: Gateway checkout 502s are consistently caused by order returning 500 on POST /v1/orders within the same correlation IDs. Gateway itself is healthy (readyz 200). Root cause is bounded to order's 500s; the specific internal mechanism needs order-side evidence.
missing_evidence: Order service logs/traces for the failing POST /v1/orders requests to identify the internal 500 cause
Order dependency metrics (postgresql, payment, inventory) to rule out db-pool-exhaustion, redis-timeout, or downstream-latency
